extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: A large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset introduced in the paper. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. The paper also states LongVid contains 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.citeAs: Li, Xinhao et al. VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574v4, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: To build LongVid, the authors leverage existing datasets including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, covering movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild long-duration videos. For data curation, they generate dense event labels for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions, filter consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence, and construct event label sequences with corresponding timestamps. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations, they directly use them as event labels; for others, they extract the major event from the caption using an LLM. They then construct long video QA pairs based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The videos of LongVid are curated from four open-source video datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. The construction also uses existing caption and annotation sources including Ego4D-HCap, HowToInterlink7M/CosMo, HT-Step, Panda-70M, and original high-quality captions provided in MiraData.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filter consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence, concatenate lower-level captions to form dense captions for some sources, extract event and background labels from captions using Qwen-72B for MiraData, and extract major events from captions using an LLM for datasets without event-level annotations. They also construct multiple QA task types from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For data curation, the authors generate dense event labels for each long video, filter consecutive segments that can be regrouped into long video sequences, construct sequences of event labels with timestamps, directly use existing event-level annotations when available, and otherwise extract major events from captions using an LLM. For HD-VILA, they filter consecutive video segments that can be reconstructed into videos longer than 60 seconds. For Ego4D, they concatenate captions across hierarchy levels to form dense captions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: LongVid annotations are created from existing high-quality short video captions and event-level annotations, plus LLM-assisted extraction. Specifically, the authors use Panda-70M captions for HD-VILA, CosMo/HowToInterlink7M captions for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap captions for Ego4D, and original high-quality captions in MiraData. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations such as HT-Step and Ego4D-HCap, they directly use them as event labels. For others, they extract major events from captions using an LLM. They then construct QA pairs for five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. For the MH-NIAH-Video benchmark, images are sourced from MS-COCO and use its human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For the MH-NIAH-Video benchmark, the paper states that MS-COCO human-annotated captions and question-answer pairs are used, but no annotator demographic details are provided.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The source data include egocentric videos, movies, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos. The paper does not explicitly specify sensitive attributes collected, but it explicitly mentions video types including egocentric videos.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that previous Needle-in-a-Video-Haystack evaluations may suffer from information leakage because images and questions similar to the needle may appear in training data. To reduce this, the proposed Multi-Hop benchmark uses MS-COCO images and wrong reasoning paths so that memorizing image content is less helpful. The paper also states that adding HD-VILA videos could enhance the model’s ability to process long videos in uncommon domains, implying source-domain coverage limitations in prior data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that one challenge in long video model training is the shortage of large-scale, high-quality data, and that existing long-form video-text datasets lack the instruction-following paradigm of (video, instruction, answer) triplets crucial for multimodal reasoning. It also notes limitations of previous NIAH-Video evaluation: possible information leakage and insufficient assessment of reasoning ability.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced as a long video instruction-tuning dataset to support models in handling diverse long video scenarios. In the training pipeline, long video data are used in Stage-3 joint short and long video instruction tuning, mixed with image and short video data so the model retains fine-grained understanding while expanding long-video comprehension. The dataset supports tasks including video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
